classification.difficultyReason: Follow equal-length markings through two isosceles triangles, using a straight-line angle between them, then transfer the roof angle by symmetry and use perpendicularity.

content.prompt:
A framework for a symmetrical roof is shown. $AD$ is perpendicular to $BC$.

Find the value of the angles marked $p$, $q$, $r$.

spec.description: Symmetrical roof ABC with vertical AD and four symmetric struts. Six matching single ticks identify the two lower roof segments and all four struts. Dotted arcs mark q at the lower left attachment, p at C, r between AD and AC, and the given 40-degree angle between the left struts. Internal coordinate names E, F, G and H are not printed.
spec.mathematics: BE=ED=FD=DG=DH=HC; angle EDF=40 degrees; B,E,F,A are collinear; A,G,H,C are collinear; AD is perpendicular to BC. Coordinates derive from equal struts at directions 145,105,75 and 35 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only p, q, r, the given 40 degrees, labels A,B,C,D and source marks are shown. No numerical answer or additional right-angle mark is supplied.

answer.worked:
The two left struts are equal, so the triangle between them is isosceles. Each angle at the roof is
$$\frac{180^{\circ}-40^{\circ}}{2}=70^{\circ}.$$
The lower roof attachment lies on a straight line:
$$\begin{align*}q&=180^{\circ}-70^{\circ}\\q&=110^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
The lower left roof segment and its adjoining strut are equal. The base angle at $B$ is
$$\frac{180^{\circ}-110^{\circ}}{2}=35^{\circ}.$$
By roof symmetry,
$$p=35^{\circ}.$$
Since $AD\perp BC$, triangle $ADC$ is right-angled:
$$\begin{align*}r&=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\r&=55^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
